tasks.title: The scheduled run is told which capabilities it holds
tasks.objective: A scheduled run receives a capability catalog built from the person-filtered inheritedToolPolicy.semanticCapabilities on its existing spawn-input field, so an agent is told which grants it holds. Entries gain an invocation union over the four usable binding kinds with a lane-neutral tool reference and, for local CLI, the reviewed argument patterns. The renderer sheds non-granted material first, never hides a grant, and fails the run closed when even names will not fit.
acceptance_criteria: The scheduled spawn input carries a catalog built from the person-filtered capability set, asserted over the real job execution path where the field is absent today
A capability active for the app but not granted to the acting person never appears as ready, asserted with the two sets differing
Rendered guidance carries display name, stable id, neutral tool reference and reviewed argument shape, asserted against exact rendered text
A descriptor is produced for each of the four usable binding kinds; the adapter reference never appears; a legacy mcp_tool binding still fails validation
The neutral reference resolves to the Anthropic tool name against the real projection including with tool search active, and the DeepAgents entry is asserted absent
No grant is hidden: shedding follows the fixed order and the derived ceiling cannot conflict with the never-hide rule
Hard overflow fails the run before any provider or tool call with a redacted capability_catalog_overflow diagnostic naming the counts
The never-hide guarantee survives both the section budget and the total prompt budget, asserted end to end through prompt compilation
A deterministic replay builds materialization through the production path and makes the dispatcher call first, with a negative control proving the descriptor causes it
The 97ded3746 block is gone, the dispatcher description points at the catalog, and its schema, risk and enforcement are pinned unchanged
No descriptor contains an executable path, hash or credential, asserted against a binding carrying all three

plan_contracts.statement: The scheduled spawn input carries a capability catalog built from inheritedToolPolicy.semanticCapabilities, not the broader snapshot set, so an app-active but ungranted capability never appears as ready.

CatalogEntry carries a closed invocation union over the four usable implementation kinds; skill actions are a tool rule distinguished by source, and a legacy mcp_tool binding never reaches the catalog.

The catalog stores a lane-neutral tool reference; an explicit mapping renders the Anthropic runtime's tool name, and the absence of a DeepAgents entry is asserted so that lane's gap cannot drift silently.

Material is shed in order (non-granted entries, then descriptions, then descriptors); the ceiling is derived as at least the compact representation of the granted set; the guarantee survives both the section and total prompt budgets.

When the compact name-and-id list exceeds the total prompt budget the run fails before any provider or tool call with a redacted capability_catalog_overflow startup diagnostic naming the granted and renderable counts.
Reviewed argument shapes render exactly as reviewed; no descriptor contains an executable path, a hash or a credential.
Enforcement is unchanged: template mismatch still refused, no classifier-derived or cached allow reaches the dispatcher, executable identity and structured argv limits still apply.

verify_commands: npx vitest run --config vitest.unit.config.ts apps/core/test/unit/agents apps/core/test/unit/runtime apps/core/test/unit/jobs apps/core/test/unit/runner

reviewer_focus: Which capability set feeds the catalog: the person-filtered set, never the broader snapshot set
That no descriptor leaks an executable path, hash or credential while reviewed argument operands are permitted
That enforcement is genuinely untouched: 0120 and 0130 proofs still green
That the never-hide guarantee is asserted through prompt compilation, not the renderer alone

review_budget.reason: Seven source files and seven test files. The source side is one builder call on the job path, an invocation union on the catalog entry, the shedding and overflow rules in the renderer and profile service, a lane mapping, one deletion and one description edit. The replay suite is the only new test machinery.
